doc.title: Kristen Korb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000

title: Eye contact and conversation on the bandstand
summary: What bassist and pianist eyebrow signals mean about changes and turnarounds.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I’ll bet. I like watching the bassist and the piano player. Sometimes they’ll like look at each other and you raise your eyes like, but what did that say to the piano player, back and forth.

Sometimes what it is, is that even if you both know the song, because jazz is such a wonderfully creative thing, a lot of times people have alternative changes for different sections. Turnarounds — do you do two-five-one, do you just go five-one, do you take it up a half step. Sometimes that’s what the eyebrow means. I’m going to go up from where you think I’m going to go. So it’s very cool. And that to me is one of the exciting things because it’s such a conversation. You have to listen to everybody in order to be in the
conversation. Listen to where they’re going and watch and the eye contact, and letting them know you’re just digging the groove or nice solo.
